title: The ninety-nine, all of them
hook: the ninety-nine names, counted on beads or on fingertips, one a day from here
tomorrow: box one of ninety-nine is empty. which name goes in it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, teach one: convey from me, even one verse, with the warning in the same breath. Pass one on. That closed al-Nawawi's forty. Today, a new block.

Click. Click. Click. A string of beads slipping through someone's fingers in the back seat of a car, at a bus stop, in a hospital waiting room. The sound is soft and steady, and what's being counted is the answer to yesterday's question. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said, in a report Bukhari and Muslim both record, in paraphrase: Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one, and whoever counts them and keeps them enters the Garden. From tomorrow, this block meets them, one a day.
screen: `CLICK. CLICK. CLICK.` → `ONE HUNDRED LESS ONE.` → `ONE A DAY.`

segments.voice: The beads have a name, misbaha, and people loop them through their fingers saying subhanallah, glory be to Allah, or the names themselves. But here's the detail to tell a friend tonight. Abu Dawud records a companion who saw the Prophet counting his glorifications on his own hand. And a woman named Yusayrah reports, in Tirmidhi's collection, that he told the women to count on their fingertips, because the fingertips will be asked, and made to speak. So in these reports, the counting tool is a hand. Feel the joints of your fingers with your thumb: there's a counter you always carry. Then the number. The hadith gives ninety-nine with a promise, but doesn't list them; the familiar list comes from a report in Tirmidhi's collection. And a du'a in Ahmad's Musnad asks Allah by every name He has, even names He kept to Himself. So ninety-nine isn't a fence around Him. The Qur'an says, in Pickthall's words: Allah's are the fairest names. Invoke Him by them. From here, a name a day, each one opened like a door.
screen: `MISBAHA: BEADS FOR COUNTING.` · `HE COUNTED ON HIS HAND.` · `FINGERTIPS WILL BE MADE TO SPEAK.` · `NINETY-NINE, AND MORE BEHIND.` · then, large: `EVERY NAME A DOOR.`

segments.voice: On a page, write the numbers one to ninety-nine in a grid, small, ten to a row. Go slowly and feel the pen move, a number for each breath if you like. If the sit ends before ninety-nine, that's fine; box one is for tomorrow's name.
screen: `ONE TO NINETY-NINE.` · `TEN TO A ROW.` · `BOX ONE WAITS.`

segments.voice: The ninety-nine: the beautiful names of Allah, counted on beads or on fingertips, one door at a time.
Keep this one: every name a door, and a whole hallway of them ahead. Talk soon.

screen: `DAY 1474 COUNTS.` → `THE NINETY-NINE NAMES · BLOCK TWO BEGINS · YEAR FIVE, 48 OF 365.` → `TOMORROW: BOX ONE OF NINETY-NINE IS EMPTY. WHICH NAME GOES IN IT?`

howItsDone: Muslims count glorifications and the names of Allah on prayer beads (misbaha or subha) or on the joints of the fingers, often after the daily prayers.

Keep them in a drawer. Beads only count if you already pray with them.

chat.meaning: The promise is for whoever counts the names and keeps them. Beads or fingertips, one name at a time is how the counting begins.

misbaha.meaning: a string of prayer beads for counting praise

Yusayrah.meaning: a woman companion who reported counting on the fingertips

Abu Dawud.meaning: a scholar whose hadith collection records the hand-counting

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 7392; Sahih Muslim 2677 (Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever counts them enters the Garden)
Sunan Abi Dawud 1502 (Abdullah ibn Amr: he saw the Prophet counting tasbih on his hand)
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3583; Sunan Abi Dawud 1501 (Yusayrah: count on your fingertips, for they will be questioned and made to speak)
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3507 (the familiar list); Musnad Ahmad 3712 (the du'a asking by every name, including those kept in the unseen)
